findings.reason: the real codex timing available is the run's stream-file mtime span or the client rollout receipt's `generation_seconds`/`machine_seconds` (`_apply_receipt_to_throughput`, `reckon/_backends.py:2639`), so §6 must name that source and label the recorded `worker_seconds_source` to match it rather than assert event-derived `stream_events`.
findings.text: §6's deliverable is "read worker time from a codex stream's own events and record `worker_seconds_source` `stream_events`", but no codex `stream.jsonl` carries any time on its events: 0 of 83 codex streams under the crew home contain a `timestamp` field, and a 2026-10-16 codex run's events carry only `{thread_id, type, item, usage}` (item payloads `reasoning`/`agent_message`/`command_execution`/`mcp_tool_call`/`file_change` have no stamp or duration; `turn.completed` carries token `usage` only). The stream measures read worker time via `cached_stream_timestamp_bounds`, which keys on `event.get("timestamp")` (`reckon/_backends.py:2621`) — the very field a claude-format stream carries and a codex stream does not (`reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:133`). So the stated mechanism cannot be satisfied from the artifact §6 names, and a node implementing it literally reaches its done-when only by inventing a different source.

findings.reason: the two are two halves of one requirement round-trip (the assessment is only weighable once §3 can condition on a stored requirement), they share all write paths and one test file, and §2's done-when proves both, so splitting is optional rather than corrective.
findings.text: §2 bundles two of §1's separate defect rows into one node: adding the `--assess` input that renders `node.orchestrator_assessment` (§1 "a coordinator's reading travels only inside --comment"), and persisting the resolved capability on the run's `node_definition` (§1 "the run does not record the requirement"), so one verdict must cover a new CLI surface and a record-writes change.
